content:
Krail aligns the punishment order once more against the edge of the table, squaring its corners with two fingers as though the paper itself might drift out of true.

"It will remain here, my lord, unsigned," he says. "The register inventory in the damaged rooms requires my attention, and the porters are waiting on my word before they move anything. I will return within the hour for your signature—or your amendment, should you wish the terms adjusted."

He does not hurry. He retrieves his pocket watch, glances at it, and closes the lid with a small click. At the door he pauses, one hand on the frame, and looks back at the room with the same level attention he gives a ledger.

"For the record, my lord: the girl has admitted the entry and the fire. The mother's responsibility follows from her keys. The folio's loss is noted separately in my report. These are three entries in one account." His thin lips press together. "Household discipline loses its force when it is delayed. I would advise deciding before the prisoners are returned to holding."

Then he is gone. The door closes without a slam—the latch catches softly, as everything in his hands does—and his measured footsteps fade down the passage toward the east wing.

The room is quieter without him, though not quiet. Wind still works at the tall west windows, carrying the smell of wet ash up from the courtyard where the fire crews are dumping their buckets. Ilyra's ruined portrait rests against the wall where it was carried, the paint bubbled and split along one side, the gilded frame scorched black at its lower corner. Her face survives in the unburned half—one eye, the curve of her cheek, a fragment of the silver tower painted behind her shoulder.

Liora shifts her weight from foot to foot. Her blistered palm is curled against her skirt, and she keeps glancing from the unsigned order to you and back, her mouth opening twice before any sound comes out. The inner red of her hair shows through the black where she has pushed it back from her face, disordered and soot-streaked.

"I didn't—" she starts, then stops herself, jaw tight, and looks down at the floor.

Elise's hand settles on her daughter's shoulder without gripping it. Her bandaged forearm is held against her body, the cloth stained brown at the center. When she speaks, her voice is level and tired.

"The young lord hasn't asked us anything yet, Liora. Wait to be asked."

Isolde stands where she has stood throughout, near your right shoulder, hands placed neatly before her apron. Her head turns a fraction toward the closed door as Krail's footsteps fade, then returns to its forward position. When she speaks, her voice is low and even, pitched for you alone.

"The physician remains in the east wing, my lord. He has not been summoned. The elder one's bandage has not been changed since the fire." A pause, no longer than a breath. "The steward's return within the hour is also noted. There is time before then, if you wish to use it."

Outside, in the passage, a floorboard creaks—the faint, held-breath sound of someone who has been standing still for a while and has just shifted their weight. Magerrett has not moved away from the door. Farther down the corridor, no second sound follows, but you know Taigar is there all the same.

Liora lifts her head. Her large reddish-brown eyes find you across the room, and for a moment the wariness in them gives way to something older—the look of a girl who once wound up a silver bird to make you laugh, and does not know what she is to you now.

The unsigned order lies on the table, the pen beside it, the approval space blank.
